strengths: The GM throws its own roll from its own list: the dice at the rules' faces, the kind, the critical, every flat source and the advantage dice are written fresh by the primary (roll-draw.mjs legalRollOf 1599-1612, drawnOptions 1585-1591, termsOf 1549-1558); the packet's roll keeps only its class and, where nothing differs, its formula, and its own options are never carried (THE GM'S OWN OPTIONS, 1560-1584).

What the draw reads is read in one step after the audit's wait (expectedFor 2359-2371: readyFor, then judgedFor, then every row with no await between), so a write that lands during a pick card's wait is judged before the dice.

A draw belongs to an action being taken: payments are tickets seen landing on this GM (notePayments 1032-1053), a draw takes one in the same tick as the last look (drawRefusal 1138-1185), a later roll of the action supersedes the older unsettled one (keepRecord 2602-2612), and two draws of one action at once are refused (drawOnGm's `drawing` lock 1301-1320).

A resend is answered from the record by Foundry's sender and the request id, never by the packet (drawAgainOf 2626-2635), so a primary that reloads between its message and its answer does not judge the roll twice.

Every roll's privacy is keyed on its subject at the last moment, and the module's own rolls are emptied of their character as they are created (private-rolls.mjs neutralRollSource 719-729, neutralRollOf 778-801, enforceContentVisibility 469-504).
Who may read a drawn roll is each browser's own set, asked before core's rule and written nowhere (readableRule 1616-1631, isReadableHere 1602-1606); nobody's whisper list names the roller.
The dice of a masked killer reach non-insiders without the roller's user id or character (maskSplit 1815-1821, used by both relays 1794 and 1875).

The window's lock is written before Daggerheart draws its context, and only where the method reads as the one read (roll-dialog.mjs wrapPrepareContext 215-246), with a said fallback; a Call armed while a window stands open waits for the next roll (windowCalls 117-128).

The Loaded Die is loaded on one roll instance's evaluate and lifted in a finally, once per purchase (forced-roll.mjs loadDie 176-227), and a die whose faces come from elsewhere is read as not held (loadedDieHeld 91-100).

A roll thrown with no GM moves nothing until a GM grants it, its stamp is held to its author owning the character and to no GM-only flag (roll-draw.mjs awayRowOf 2836-2848), and the grant is decided on the primary, one decision at a time (askToDecide 2955-2959, decideUnwitnessed 2944-2948).
No function in the seven files is over 150 lines (the longest: whisperRoll 118, throwDrawn 106, onRenderApplication 102), and each wait is a named constant marked chosen or measured.
dice-look.mjs is read-only: a player's run reads its own User alone and none of the GMs' store (lookView 339-380).

findings.title: A hindering Call is thrown and spent on the supporting rolls of Pick the Lock, Tail Someone and Take from the Body on the GM, while the roller's window and the GM's own road shield them
findings.where: scripts/roll-draw.mjs:1857 (SPENDS_NO_CALL holds "palm" alone), 1865-1869 (hostileCalls), 1673-1675 and 1715-1716 (throwDrawn applies and spends them); scripts/action-pipeline.mjs:155-157 (rollTrait shields every `remember: false` roll but the opening); scripts/action-doors.mjs:143, scripts/action-tail.mjs:81, scripts/anonymity.mjs:546 and 561 (the three supporting rolls with an action key)
findings.what_happens: rollTrait on the roller's browser shields every `remember: false` roll except an opening (`supporting = !remember && !calls.TAKES_CALLS.has(actionKey)`), so the window of Pick the Lock's cover (`pickCover`), Tail Someone's notice roll (`tailUnseen`) and a Take's cover (`lootCover`) opens with no Call, and the packet names none. On the primary, hostileCalls returns [] only for a key in SPENDS_NO_CALL or for no key at all; these three keys are neither, so every hindering Call armed on the character more than HOSTILE_GRACE (60 s) before the draw - a Monokuma's Obstacle, a Meddle's -1 - is thrown into the supporting roll and spent with it (`used = [...applied, ...hostile]`). The claim lacks that die, so checkRoll raises an `advantage` (or `modifier`) flag and the GMs get the 'did not match' whisper for an honest roll; rollerLine tells the roller nothing (the claim had nothing extra). The Call is then gone before the action's own roll (`pick`, `tail`, `loot`), which it was bought for. SPENDS_NO_CALL's own comment (1853-1856) says it mirrors rollTrait's `remember: false`, and the note at 1813-1815 says such a roll 'is given none'; the three keys came later (E68 C10, E69 C3, E74 C4) and were not added.
findings.failure_scenario: A Monokuma buys an Obstacle on Aiko; two minutes later Aiko picks a lock with a witness in the room: her cover window shows no disadvantage, the GM throws the cover at disadvantage and whispers the GMs that her roll 'did not match', and the lock's Hand roll that follows is thrown with no Obstacle at all.
findings.expected: The drawn road gives a supporting roll the Calls the roller's road gives it - none but an opening's - so the Obstacle waits for the action's own roll and a legal road raises no flag (the trust model's layer two, scenario 83's rule).
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a shield on the GM's side: armedCallsShown (call-effects.mjs:202-205) reads the flag and the Confusions with no `shielded` test, and the GM's module-level shield is 0 while it draws someone else's roll. Looked for another gate on these keys in throwDrawn and expectedFor: none (situationReading answers 0 for them, the `calls` row is 0, the `hostile` row carries the dice). Looked for a test that pins the opposite: git grep finds no tier-2 or scenario test that arms a hindering Call before a pickCover, tailUnseen or lootCover roll; scenario 83's Obstacle (223-230, 378-381) is thrown on a statistic from the sheet, where the hostile row is meant to apply. The GM's own road (a GM driving the sheet) shields on its own browser, so the two roads disagree. Not run.
findings.tests_near: Tier 2 tests read by their comments at scripts/tests-tier2.mjs:9814, 9862, 10009 (hostile Calls named and unnamed on action rolls) and 18091, 18175 (E112's opening); none drives a supporting roll with an action key.

findings.title: With 'Lock the roll window for players' off, the window hands a student the statistic, the Experiences and the bonus box, and the GM's draw counts none of them: every use is flagged to the GMs and told to the roller as not counted
findings.where: scripts/roll-dialog.mjs:351-401 (the lock-off branch) and its note at 366-370; scripts/roll-draw.mjs:1517-1536 (scoredOf: experiences only as far as an Experience Call bought, the rest clamped into the effects' range), 2414-2427 (checkRoll), 1621-1638 (rollerLine); scripts/settings-window.mjs:91 (the switch is drawn there)
findings.what_happens: The lock-off branch imposes what a Call bought and leaves 'which trait, which experience, the roll mode, the free-text bonus' to the player (roll-dialog.mjs:368-370). Since E29 C10 the primary throws its own list: an Experience without a Talent/Experience Call is not counted (`experiences.slice(0, expected.experiences)`, the row's bound 0 without the Call), a typed bonus is clamped into the character's effects' range, and a statistic other than the action's is not thrown. So with the switch off, a player who ticks an Experience or types a bonus sees the window's formula include it, the GM throws without it, checkRoll records `modifier` (or `trait`), the GMs get the 'did not match' whisper and the roller gets 'The GM counted ...; not counted: ...'. The switch's own hint ('Players cannot change ... Experiences, or bonus') describes only the on state; nothing on the off state says these controls no longer count.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM turns the lock off so players can drive their windows; a player ticks the Experience that fits her Search and rolls: her window showed +2, the card shows the total without it, she is told 'not counted: modifier +2', and the GMs read a flagged roll from an honest player.
findings.expected: Either the off state leaves only what the draw counts (the mode, a statistic for a roll whose action names none), or the switch's text says that what the player picks there is a claim the GM does not count.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked that the switch is reachable: settings.mjs:3123-3130 registers it with config: false, but settings-window.mjs:91 draws it in the module's own settings window, and the GM handbook (line 91) lists it. Checked whether the draw counts a window's Experience without a Call: the `experience` reader answers row.bound (1) only when an applied Call grants `experience` (roll-draw.mjs:2289). Checked a statistic from the sheet: there the roller's statistic stands (traitFrom null, `trait = expected.trait ?? claim.trait`), so this does not cover a sheet roll's statistic. The default is on, which is why this is minor. Not run.

findings.title: A player's dice look diagnostic reads the newest roll in the log, another student's hidden one included, and shows its author and its dice in the window it asks them to send the GM
findings.where: scripts/dice-look.mjs:325-329 (rollMessage: `gm || m.visible !== false`), 365-378 (`by = message.author?.id`, throwLook of its dice), 476-480 (the 'Roll:' line), 512 (the player's intro asks them to copy it to the GM)
findings.what_happens: With no message id, a player's run picks the newest message with rolls whose `visible` is not false. Foundry's ChatMessage#visible answers true for every whispered message that holds a roll (private-rolls.mjs:452-458 states it; the harness models it so, audit/harness/lib/shim.mjs:953-960) - only `isContentVisible` hides it. So a player's run reads the newest roll whoever it is about, and the window and console print 'Roll: <author> - hope d12: ..., advantage d6 ...' with the dice's classes, faces and modifiers (how many advantage or disadvantage dice, `kh`). For a roll not drawn (a Monocub's Meddle in another room, a roll thrown with no GM, Daggerheart's own item roll) the author is the other player; for a drawn one it is the GM, which still says that a roll was made. The module hides such a card whole because 'Kaede rolled something is itself information' (private-rolls.mjs:465-467).
findings.failure_scenario: The GM asks every player to run game.drpg.diagnoseDiceLook() after a Monocub's Meddle in the kitchen; a player in the library reads 'The roll read: <the Monocub's player> - hope d12 ...' about a roll whose card is hidden from her.
findings.expected: A player's run reads only a roll this browser may read (`isContentVisible`, or the module's own `isReadableHere`), as its own comment says.
findings.refutation_tried: Every browser holds the document, so a console learns nothing new; the finding is about the module's own window showing an honest player what the chat log hides from them. Looked for a later filter: lookView and viewLines print the roll as read; no isContentVisible test anywhere in dice-look.mjs (git grep). Foundry's own getter is not on this machine: its behaviour is the module's own note and the harness's model. Not run.

findings.title: A player who reloads while the GM draws their statistic from the sheet never reads that roll's card: the GM settles it, and the card is hidden on the roller's own browser for good
findings.where: scripts/roll-draw.mjs:595-621 (playBack: `readHere(messageId, { keep: true })` only at the answer); scripts/private-rolls.mjs:1547-1556 and 1581-1592 (readHere keep, refillReadable reads only kept ids), 1594-1606 (drawsAwaited, memory only), 1790 (relayDrawnDice leaves the roller out)
findings.what_happens: A statistic from the sheet the GM drew is the GM's message whispered to the GMs (claimed, keepCard). Its roller reads it through `drawsAwaited` while the draw is under way and through `readableHere` once the answer is played back, where `keep` writes the id to the client setting `readableRolls`. A reload between the GM's message and the answer loses both: the answer goes to a browser that is gone, playBack never runs, the id is never kept, and relayDrawnDice sends `dice.show` to the audience less the roller (`id !== by?.id`). After the reload refillReadable finds nothing for it, and enforceContentVisibility hides the card. The GM has already written its Hope or Fear step (throwDrawn 1710-1713). Wider than this file: an action's roll in the same window leaves its pipeline dead on the reloaded browser with the payment taken (the action's own abort never runs).
findings.failure_scenario: A GM asks for a Body reaction; the player clicks it and her tab reloads while the GM waits on the audit; she comes back to a log with no card of that roll, and rolls again.
findings.expected: The roller can read every roll the GM drew for them (the owner's 27.09 rule the r2-H7 note cites), after a reload too.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for another road that makes the roller's message readable: startOnMessage starts dice only; signAsRoller heads a card already readable; showRelayedDice runs readHere only for recipients of dice.show, which exclude `by`. The window is the draw's own: up to PAY_WAIT_MS, PICK_WAIT_MS and the audit's wait on the GM, so it is short but not empty. Whether a reload in that window happens at a table is not measured.

findings.title: The GMs' card of rolls thrown with no GM is posted again at every ready of the primary while one stands undecided, and a second GM's copy keeps live buttons after the primary decided
findings.where: scripts/roll-draw.mjs:2915-2930 (askAboutUnwitnessed lists every undecided stamp in the log and posts a card, no look for a card already standing); scripts/module.mjs:421 (called at every ready); roll-draw.mjs:3034-3056 (onRenderUnwitnessed removes the buttons only at a render, and on the clicking browser)
findings.what_happens: Each load of the primary GM posts one more 'Rolls with no GM connected' card for the same undecided rolls, so a GM who reloads twice before deciding has three. A decision updates the rolls' messages, not the card: on another GM's browser the card is not redrawn and its Grant all / Grant none stay; a press there asks the primary, which finds every roll decided (awayRowOf null) and answers [] - nothing is said.
findings.failure_scenario: A player rolled with nobody connected; the GM reloads twice while setting up the session and finds three identical cards in chat; the second GM presses Grant all on an old one after the first GM already did and sees nothing happen.
findings.expected: One card per undecided set (or the earlier card redrawn), and a press on a decided card says it was decided.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a dedupe of the card (a flag check, a message search for `awayCard`): none in askAboutUnwitnessed or its caller. The decision itself is safe: it runs once on the primary's queue (decideUnwitnessed). Not run.

findings.title: The GMs' whisper of a flagged roll says 'These parts did not count' also for a die or a bonus the GM threw and the window lacked
findings.what_happens: checkRoll records every difference in both directions: a claim of more than the GM counted, and a GM's number above the claim (an `advantage` flag where the GM threw a hindering Call's die or a Night's die the window did not show, a `modifier` flag where the GM counted a Call's bonus the window lacked, a `pick` flag where no card came). The one sentence over the list says each 'did not count', which is true only of the first kind; the second kind is a part the GM did count. rollerLine already tells the roller only the first kind (1626).
findings.evidence:
en.json DRPG.Rolls.unexpected: "{name}'s roll did not match the roll the GM expected, so the GM rolled the expected one. These parts did not count: {list}. game.drpg.rollFlags() lists it."
roll-draw.mjs:2423      if (claim.advantage !== scored.advantage) {
findings.failure_scenario: With finding 1's Obstacle, the GMs read 'These parts did not count: advantage dice 0, expected -1 (the GM counted: a hindering Call armed before the roll)' - a die that was counted.
findings.expected: The whisper says the GM threw its own numbers and lists the differences, without saying each 'did not count'.
findings.refutation_tried: flagText (2444-2453) builds each line as '{what} {claimed}, expected {expected}' with no direction; the header sentence is the only frame. Not run.

findings.title: On the primary, every actor flag write below full Gamemaster schedules a dice-look put-back and the switches' comparison, whether or not it touches Dice So Nice's flags
findings.where: scripts/dice-sync.mjs:214-216 (updateActor with any `changes.flags`), 957-976 (onActorWritten: `touched` decides only for a full Gamemaster), 290-292 (switchesMoved, with worldCopyMoved's stableJson of the world copy at 408-417)
findings.what_happens: A write by a player or an Assistant of any flag of any actor reaches onActorWritten with `touched` false and still runs afterSwitchesHeld (four settings compared, and the world copy of every actor's overlay stringified) and a 400 ms timer per actor, after which putBackOverlay compares that actor's overlay and role looks with the store's. The module's own flags on a student move often (Calls, notes, marks a player's browser writes). Each pass is small and nothing is written when nothing moved.
findings.failure_scenario: During a busy Investigation the primary GM's browser compares the dice-look switches and stringifies the world copy at every player flag write, for writes that cannot have moved a look.
findings.expected: A write that does not touch `flags.dice-so-nice` schedules nothing (a `noHook` write is caught at the next message anyway, checkMessage 1101-1113).
findings.refutation_tried: The schedule may be meant as a catch for a write that reaches the overlay in a shape touchesLook misses; touchesLook reads the hook's expanded diff, where any write of the overlay carries the `dice-so-nice` key. Not measured: the counters of scenario 86 do not name this path.

If the build goes on first, a statistic from the sheet sends `calls: []` and a Call the window applied is not counted (flagged `advantage`, the roller told 'not counted').

l1.what: Whether a Call a player's roll window applied is named in the drawn packet.
recipe: 1. As a player, buy a Support on your own character (or have one armed by another player).
2. Click a statistic on the sheet; the window opens with the advantage chip held.
4. As the GM, run game.drpg.rollFlags() and read the roll's record (game.drpg debug or rollStore) for `used.calls`.
l1.settles_if: the record names the Support's nonce and no `advantage` flag: the close hook ran first; no nonce and a flag: the build went on first.
